purpose: Define callisto init's generated GitHub Actions release workflow for workspaces with no build-matrix need: the file's path, no-overwrite/dry-run rules, the two-job version-pr/release shape, callisto-action's new mode input, and the fix to callisto-action's internal setup-callisto reference required for the action to run when invoked from outside this repository.
scope: Workflow generation triggered by SPEC-DX-SETUP-CORE's --workflow/--no-workflow flags or interactive question, for a workspace with no napi/maturin platform packages (per IdentityIndex::attached_platforms) and no [[release.artifact]] slots: the generated file's path, the no-overwrite error and its interaction with --dry-run, the --workflow/--no-workflow mutual-exclusivity error, the two-job content (trigger, permissions, secrets, pinned action reference), callisto-action's mode input and its outputs, and callisto-action's internal setup-callisto reference fix. Depends on SPEC-DX-SETUP-CORE for the triggering question/flags and the ResolvedConfig facts that route generation to this spec instead of SPEC-DX-SETUP-WORKFLOW-MATRIX. Depends on SPEC-DX-RELEASE-CLI for callisto release's own execution-time idempotency, which AC-004a relies on instead of reintroducing gating in the workflow, and for the `callisto release` invocation AC-003a's release-mode step runs.
non_goals: The build-matrix workflow shape for workspaces with napi/maturin platform packages or [[release.artifact]] slots -- SPEC-DX-SETUP-WORKFLOW-MATRIX's territory, which depends on this spec's mode input and per-job permission/secret model rather than redefining them.
init's detection, questions, non-interactive flags beyond --workflow/--no-workflow, and config write -- SPEC-DX-SETUP-CORE's territory.
callisto release's own flag surface and CI-split mechanics -- SPEC-DX-RELEASE-CLI's territory.

A recovery-job, coordinator-job, or any SHA-based release-candidate-detection step -- explicitly excluded by design, not merely undesigned; callisto release's own execution-time idempotency is relied on instead.
Editing or migrating a workflow file that already exists at the target path -- init refuses to touch it (AC-002a) rather than merging or updating it.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: init generates a workflow file only when the operator answers yes to the interactive 'Generate a GitHub Actions release workflow? (y/N)' question or supplies --workflow non-interactively.

When workflow generation is not requested (answered no, or --no-workflow / omitted under --yes, per SPEC-DX-SETUP-CORE AC-015's default-not-generated rule), no file under .github/workflows/ is created or modified by init.
A generated workflow file is written to .github/workflows/callisto-release.yml (callisto_model::RELEASE_COORDINATOR_WORKFLOW_PATH, the one workflow release artifact attestations are bound to).

The .github/workflows/callisto-release.yml existence check runs before any preview is shown, including under --dry-run. When a file already exists there, init errors naming that existing file instead of overwriting it, and writes nothing, in both normal and --dry-run runs.
Supplying --workflow and --no-workflow together errors naming both flags as mutually exclusive; no workflow file is written and the interactive question is not asked.

callisto-action's action.yml gains a mode input accepting version-pr or release, defaulting to version-pr so an existing workflow that omits the input keeps its current create-or-update-release-PR behavior unchanged.
When mode is release, callisto-action installs the callisto environment and runs callisto release instead of the version-pr script.

When mode is release, callisto-action's published and publishedPackages outputs are populated from the callisto release receipt rather than the fixed 'false' / '[]' values the version-pr mode still produces.
Supplying a mode value other than version-pr or release errors naming version-pr and release as the accepted values; no release or version-pr step runs.

For a workspace with no build-matrix need, the generated file has 40 or fewer lines, contains exactly two jobs -- one invoking callisto-action with mode omitted or set to version-pr for release-PR creation, and one invoking callisto-action with mode: release on push to the default branch -- and both jobs reference callisto-action as uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/callisto-action@callisto@<version>, pinned to the callisto version running init.

In the no-build-matrix generated file, neither job contains a recovery-job, coordinator-job, or SHA-based release-candidate-detection step; the release job carries no commit-SHA gating and relies on callisto release's own execution-time idempotency to no-op on a redundant run.
The generated workflow's push trigger targets the repository's default branch, detected from origin/HEAD at generation time and falling back to main when origin/HEAD cannot be resolved.
The version-pr job declares permissions contents: write and pull-requests: write; the release job declares permissions contents: write and id-token: write.

The release job's secrets are wired per detected ecosystem: CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN when the workspace has a cargo package, NPM_TOKEN when it has an npm package, PYPI_TOKEN when it has a PyPI package; a workspace with no packages for an ecosystem gets no secret wired for it.

callisto-action's composite step that installs the callisto environment references setup-callisto as uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/setup-callisto@<pinned-ref> instead of the current uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto, so a generated workflow in a consumer repository that invokes callisto-action externally can resolve and run that nested step.

revision_note: Split from SPEC-DX-SETUP-WORKFLOW per GATE2-FIXES.md's SPEC-DX-SETUP-WORKFLOW section into the no-build-matrix half; the build-matrix half moved to SPEC-DX-SETUP-WORKFLOW-MATRIX, which now depends on this spec's mode input, permission model, and secret wiring instead of redefining them. Corrections applied, each an owner judgment call recorded here: (1) AC-002a now states explicitly that the existing-file check runs before the preview and under --dry-run, per GATE2-FIXES.md -- previously only the overwrite refusal was stated, not its ordering relative to --dry-run. (2) New AC-002b: --workflow/--no-workflow are mutually exclusive; assigned to this spec (the workflow-generation entry point) rather than SPEC-DX-SETUP-CORE (which owns general flag parsing), a judgment call made to keep the one error condition in the spec whose acceptance criteria it gates, rather than splitting it across two specs. (3) New AC-003b/AC-003c: release-mode output population and the invalid-mode error, both named in GATE2-FIXES.md but absent from the prior AC-003/AC-003a pair. (4) AC-004 now states the exact pinned uses: reference (orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/callisto-action@callisto@<version>) and new AC-004b/AC-004c/AC-004d add the push-trigger default-branch detection, per-job permissions, and per-ecosystem secret wiring -- all taken verbatim from GATE2-FIXES.md rather than re-derived. (5) New AC-005: callisto-action's internal uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto step reference is non-portable outside this repository -- confirmed present verbatim in .github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml on origin/main via git show -- and must become the full external path per GATE2-FIXES.md ('make setup-callisto referenceable externally... not $/'); this is a fix to the action's own definition, not just to generated workflow content. Path change (owner decision, wave 7b): the generated file moved from .github/workflows/release.yml to .github/workflows/callisto-release.yml so build-matrix artifacts attested by it pass release execute's signer-workflow check; one name for both generated shapes.
reasoning: No api_surface: interface is a generated YAML file and a GitHub Action's declared inputs, not a callable code signature. mode input's absence today and callisto-action's setup-callisto step reference were confirmed via git show origin/main:.github/actions/callisto-action/action.yml, which has no mode input, always runs create-or-update-release-pr.sh, and contains uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto verbatim. Trust model (owner-default decision, wave 7b review): a merge to the protected default branch is the release approval, as in prior art; init states it after writing the workflow (workflow-merge-publishes info diagnostic) instead of generating an environment or reviewer gate.
